text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 10.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica'; text-anchor: start; fill: #141414

g.text: Both engines are permutation tests — what actually differs is the family and the statistic
model7 · n = 58 · 5000 permutations each · same contrast images, same mask (59,838 voxels), nilearn patched to 18-connectivity
SnPM's one-tailed-per-tail family is the more permissive of the two.
The Shannon-surprise clusters sit right on the boundary: their nilearn
two-tailed cluster-EXTENT p is .071 and .054 — not significant — while
cluster MASS gives .048 and .021, and SnPM's one-tailed family puts
them under .05. Same data, three defensible procedures, opposite
The RPE and uRPE maps are indifferent to all of this. The surprise map
is not, and neither is the small uRPE-positive set.
Across the 23 signal × sign × threshold panels where both engines
return a map, 16 agree to the voxel (Dice > 0.995). Where they
disagree it is always a marginal effect, and the cause is the family,
Signed RPE neg, p < 0.001: SnPM 88 vox vs nilearn 0
Shannon surprise pos, p < 0.01: SnPM 616 vox vs nilearn 0
Shannon surprise pos, p < 0.005: SnPM 894 vox vs nilearn 0
